plan.english: Sons of Sky, come to me!

notes: The twins' title 'sons of Sky': Ved. Divó nápātā (RV 1.117.12, 1.182.1, 4.44.2, 10.61.4 'come to me, Aśvins, grandsons of Dyaus'), Gk Διόσκουροι / Δίος παῖδες (Alcaeus fr. 34 'come to me, sons of Zeus'). The genitive of *dyḗws is shared by Vedic and Greek; Lith. Diẽvo sūnẽliai and Latv. Dieva dēli have *deywós (Diẽvas 'god'), not *dyḗws, so the Baltic ref is support only. The word for 'son' is renewed in each branch (nápāt- 'descendant', παῖδες, sūnẽliai, dēli), so suHnús is interpolated. 'Come' is the Vedic root aorist ā́ gatam (gʷémt, interpolated; Alcaeus has δεῦτε). The enclitic *moy (Ved. me = Gk μοι) is a real shared form, but the builder does not credit closed-class tokens. Dual as in Vedic. RV 10.61.4 checked locally; Alcaeus (wording after West) and the dainos are not in local corpora.

plan.english: The daughter of the Sun chose the chariot of you two.

notes: The Sun's daughter and her twin suitors: Vedic duhitā́ sū́ryasya chose the Aśvins' chariot (RV 1.117.13 yuvó rátham duhitā́ sū́ryasya ... avr̥ṇīta) or the Aśvins as husbands (1.119.5, 7.69.4: support); in the Baltic songs Lith. Sáulės dukrýtė, Latv. Saules meita is wooed by the Sons of God (West 2007 ch. 5). Shared is the NP 'daughter of the Sun' (Ved. duhitár- = Lith. duktė̃, here the diminutive dukrýtė; Latv. meita is not cognate). The verb (*welh₁-, Ved. middle aorist), the chariot (Hróth₂os, Ved. rátha-) and 'of you two' are Vedic only, interpolated. Revised: the clause 'chose you two as husbands' had been stitched from RV 1.119.5 onto 7.69.4; the line now follows one stanza. RV 1.117.13, 7.69.4 and 1.119.5 checked locally; the dainos are not in local corpora.

plan.english: The two sons of Sky came, asking for the daughter of the Sun.

notes: The Sons of Sky as suitors of the Sun's daughter: RV 10.85.14 the Aśvins came 'asking for' (pr̥chámānau, middle participle) Sūryā's wedding; RV 1.117.12–13 (two stanzas of one hymn) call them Divó nápātā (12) and name duhitā́ sū́ryasya (13); in Latvian songs Dieva dēli are suitors of Saule's daughter (West 2007 ch. 5). Only 'daughter of the Sun' is shared with Baltic (Ved. duhitā́ sū́ryasya = Lith. Sáulės dukrýtė). Lith. Diẽvo sūnẽliai is *deywós + a diminutive of *suHnús and is not cognate with divó nápātā, so dyḗws and suHnús are Vedic or interpolated here. Interpolated: pr̥sḱéti (Ved. pr̥ccha-; Latv. precinieks 'suitor' < *preḱ- is not printed by West), 'came' (root aorist of *gʷem-; Ved. áyātam is from yā-). Middle participle as in Vedic. RV 10.85.14 and 1.117.12–13 checked locally; the dainos are not in local corpora.

plan.english: Come to us with swift horses!

notes: The inherited 'swift horses' (*h₁ōḱéwes h₁éḱwōs, Watkins 1995: 12): RV 8.5.7 'come, Aśvins, with swift horses' and Homeric ὠκέας ἵππους (Il. 5.275 'the two came near, driving swift horses', a dual subject); both checked locally. As the review advised, the Homeric phrase replaces Alcaeus' compound ὠκυπόδων ἵππων of the Dioskouroi (fr. 34; support only, not in local corpora). Interpolated: the verb yā- 'travel, go' of the Vedic (yéh₂ti, Ved. yāti, Lith. jóti 'ride'; Gk ἦλθον is another root) and 'to us'; the Vedic instrumental is kept.

plan.english: Come, you two of good horses!

notes: The twins' epithet *h₁su-h₁éḱwo- 'having good horses' (West 2007 ch. 4): Ved. su-áśva- of the Aśvins (sváśvā ... ā́ yātam 'come, you two of good horses', RV 7.69.3; again 7.68.1, support), Gk εὔιπποι of the Tyndaridai (Pind. Ol. 3.39, from West; not in local corpora; Homer has it only as the name Εὔιππος, Il. 16.417), and Av. huuaspa- of Mithra (Yt. 10.76 = CAB YtMihr20.5 huuaspō ahi 'you are good-horsed'; same branch as Vedic, support). Revised: the compound was decomposed into a phrase ('the sons of Sky have good horses' with h₁wésus); it is now the engine's bahuvrihi h₁suh₁éḱwos, vocative dual as in Vedic, and 'sons of Sky' is dropped (Pindar's Tyndaridai do not carry Zeus' name). The builder cannot credit compound tokens as secure (their lex_id has no lexicon entry), so no token is verified; h₁éḱwos is listed so that the check records its member in both branches (the lemmas give the compound and its second member). Interpolated: the verb yā- (Ved. yātam; the Greek has no verb). RV 7.69.3, 7.68.1, Il. 16.417 and Yt. 10.76 checked locally.

plan.english: The two sons of Sky are young.

notes: The twins are youths: Ved. yúvānā (RV 1.117.14, 3.58.7, 6.62.4, 7.67.10) beside Divó nápātā in the same hymn; the Dioskouroi are Διὸς κοῦροι 'Zeus' boys' and appear to the Romans as iuuenes (West 2007 ch. 4). Ved. yúvan- and Lat. iuuenis are the same n-stem (h₂yéwHō); the Greek word for 'boy' is different. Dual as in Vedic; 'son' as in divine-twins-001. RV 1.117.12 and 1.117.14 (two stanzas of one hymn) checked locally; the Homeric Hymn and Cicero are not in local corpora.

plan.english: Sons of Sky, you two carried him in ships.

notes: Rescuers at sea: the Aśvins carried Bhujyu out of the sea 'with ships' (naubhíḥ, RV 1.116.3, cf. the hundred-oared ship nā́vam of 1.116.5), and the Dioskouroi leap onto the masts of ships and bring light to the dark ship (Alcaeus fr. 34; Hymn. Hom. 33; West 2007 ch. 4). *néh₂us is shared; the Vedic verb vah- (*weǵʰ-, Ved. ūhathuḥ perfect, here the past of the present) and 'him' are interpolated. The Greek has no verb of carrying. The Alcaeus wording (νάων, νᾶϊ) follows West's citation (he prints a translation); it is not in a local corpus. Only *néh₂us is shared; 'rescuers at sea' is thematic, and 'sons of Sky' comes from another stanza (RV 1.117.12, support). RV 1.116.3 and 1.117.12 checked locally; Alcaeus is not in local corpora.

plan.english: The two young men came with white horses.

notes: The twin youths and their horses: RV 1.117.14 'you two young ones ... carried (Bhujyu) with swift horses', and the Roman epiphany of Castor and Pollux as two iuuenes with white horses (Cic. Nat. deor. 2.6; West 2007 ch. 4 n. 77: their horses are always white). Ved. yúvan- = Lat. iuuenis and Ved. áśva- = Lat. equus. 'White' follows the Latin (albʰós; the Vedic white horse of RV 1.116.6 is śvetá-), and 'came' (gʷémt) is interpolated; the Latin wording is cited after West's reference, not checked in a local corpus. RV 1.117.14 checked locally; Cicero is not in local corpora (late prose report). The line is a pairing of two words (h₂yéwHō, h₁éḱwos) around a Latin-only image.
